subject: Zealandia continent map
title: What If Earth Had an Eighth Continent? It Does, and 95% Is Underwater

scenes.text: What if Earth had an eighth continent? It already does. Ninety-five percent of it is underwater.
Zealandia covers 4.9 million square kilometres, about the size of India, six times Madagascar.
Roughly 80 million years ago it tore away from Gondwana, stretched so thin that most of it sank beneath the waves.
Only New Zealand and New Caledonia poke above the sea. They are the mountain tops of a drowned land.
In 2017, eleven geologists argued in the journal GSA Today that it passes every test of a continent.
By 2023 its geology was mapped out to its underwater edges, the first continent ever fully charted. And almost nobody can stand on it.

description:
What if Earth had an eighth continent? Zealandia is about 4.9 million square kilometres, roughly 95 percent of it below the sea, with New Zealand and New Caledonia as its highest peaks.
It split from Gondwana roughly 80 million years ago; in 2017 geologists made the formal case in GSA Today that it is a continent, and in 2023 GNS Science finished mapping its geology to the underwater edges.

first_comment: Zealandia's crust is only 10 to 30 kilometres thick, which is why it sank. Should maps show eight continents? And what should we run through next?
